thread:
Eli (Support): Zoe from Acme reporting large p99 latency spikes + occasional 503s from Dedicated pool eu-west-1-pool-3. Started ~2025-11-02 15:22 UTC during traffic burst. Sample request id: req_9a3f7b. Customer says some requests hit 5-8s and some timed out. Can SRE look?

Miguel (SRE): Looking now. can you paste the exact request ids + timestamps you have? also any error payloads from the client?

Eli (Support): pasted two sample ids: req_9a3f7b (15:21:47), req_c2d44f (15:23:05). Client saw "context deadline exceeded" and then 503. No auth failures.

Miguel (SRE): quick check on infra metrics: pool eu-west-1-pool-3 shows sustained queue length spike starting 15:20 -> 15:26, autoscaler triggered scale-up around 15:21 and again 15:24. New instances took ~40-80s to become ready. Model load times adding ~25-50s when a new GPU comes up (cold GPU). Combined that's inline with observed p99s. Looks like pool saturated and scale-up lagged.

Miguel (SRE): commands i ran:
```
# fetch pool metrics (support-only)
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ 
  'https://internal-metrics.redwood/eu-west-1/pools/eu-west-1-pool-3?range=30m' | jq .

# check autoscaler config
kubectl get deployment pool-autoscaler-eu-west-1-pool-3 -o yaml
```

Priya (Runtime): fwiw runtime notes: this model variant (open-100b-int8) uses large kv caches; when a node is cold we need to warm the KV cache which adds tail latency. quant+fp16 variants load faster. Also container init + CUDA context establishment is ~6-12s then model mmap/weight init is the bulk.

Priya (Runtime): we have two levers: pre-warmed standby workers (keep some replicas spun with model loaded but paused) or reduce model load by serving a lighter variant during spikes and upgrading later. We can also enable background warmers that fetch popular prefixes to populate KV cache after node comes up.

Nate (Oncall): immediate mitigations we can do right now: 1) bump min_replicas for the pool from 1 -> 3 (low risk, short cost hit), 2) enable short-lived prewarm workers (if config flag exists for that pool), 3) add temporary routing rule to send traffic to hosted fallback model (redwood-medium) for customer critical routes to avoid timeouts.

Eli (Support): Zoe — can we get approval for temporary scaling?

Zoe (Acme): yes please increase replicas, this is impacting checkout. do whatever urgent is needed.

Miguel (SRE): I'll make the change and monitor. Plan:
- set min_replicas=3 for eu-west-1-pool-3
- add a 30s warmup job to run after new instance ready to prime KV cache
- change autoscaler cooldown to 30s for scale-up (was 120s) to respond faster
- create a warmup synthetic traffic job (low qps) in the pool for 12 hours to flatten p99s while we evaluate longterm config

Miguel (SRE): scaling API we use (ops only):
```bash
curl -X POST \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_ADMIN' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  https://api.redwood.internal/v1/admin/pools/eu-west-1-pool-3/scale \ 
  -d '{"min_replicas":3, "scale_up_cooldown":30}'
```

Priya (Runtime): config snippet for prewarm (example):
```json
{
  "pool": "eu-west-1-pool-3",
  "prewarm": {
    "enabled": true,
    "replicas": 2,
    "warmup_script": "warm_kv_prefixes.sh"
  }
}
```

Miguel (SRE): note: prewarm will cost ~2 GPU-hours/hr while active. expected to reduce cold-start tail by ~60-80%. We'll monitor p95/p99. Also worth tuning autoscaler target util from 70% -> 55% for this pool if traffic is bursty.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-1129 (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2025-1129) — assigned to Miguel (SRE) and Nate (Oncall).

Eli (Support): I notified Acme that we're scaling now and enabled fallback routing for checkout endpoints. will confirm with them once p99 drops.

Miguel (SRE): done: min_replicas set to 3 at 15:27 UTC, prewarm job injected, cooldown reduced. Early signs: queue length dropped, p99 went from ~6.2s -> 1.4s over next 4 minutes. continuing to monitor.

Priya (Runtime): follow-ups: add synthetic warmers to CI so new pools come up primed; add metric for "model_ready_and_kv_warmed" that autoscaler can wait on before counting replica as ready; evaluate switching to faster-loading variant for checkout route fallback.

Nate (Oncall): next steps documented in INC-2025-1129. Miguel will prepare playbook steps to prevent regression: recommended defaults -> min_replicas>=2 for any pool with >=30% bursty traffic, autoscaler cooldown <=45s for scale-up, prewarm option enabled for large models.

Eli (Support): Acme confirms improvement, checkout failures stopped. Closing customer escalation once post-incident review done.

Miguel (SRE): assigning follow-up ticket to runtime team for warming APIs and to product for conservative default autoscaler policies. I'll post a short writeup in eng-sre channel after postmortem. :thumbsup:

Zoe (Acme): thanks everyone, appreciate the quick fix.
